title: Fever players address additional public scrutiny of playing with Caitlin Clark, while GM defends fans - CBS Sports
description: Former Fever forward Brianna Turner, however, said that players have 'repeatedly' complained about the fanbase
body:
Former Fever forward Brianna Turner, however, said that players have 'repeatedly' complained about the fanbase
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Oct 4, 2026
                            
                    at
    4:46 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            2 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        Indiana Fever players get to take the court with Caitlin Clark, but that comes with extra scrutiny and pressure as well."I don't think people really understand how much we endure, man," Fever star Kelsey Mitchell said over the weekend during exit interviews following the team's Game 3 loss to the Las Vegas Aces in the first round of the WNBA playoffs. "Like, if I showed y'all my DMs about the hate and all of the stuff that comes with being a professional athlete, but specifically being an Indiana Fever basketball player, it's a lot that goes into that. And those days are hard as hell, man."Playing with (Caitlin Clark) and having the eyes that she's got (on her), we get a lot of flak just from being on her team. I think that that comes with a lot too. And I just think that people (have) got to give us grace. I think this organization is unbelievable, man. But I think that when it comes to, like, really trying to be yourself, it hasn't always been easy."Fan behavior became a topic of discussion last week, after Aces star A'ja Wilson got into a confrontation with a Fever fan in the fourth quarter of the Aces' Game 2 loss at Gainbridge Fieldhouse. After getting entangled with Fever guard Sophie Cunningham, Wilson walked towards a man pointing at her from his seat behind the basket. Wilson was given a technical foul for the interaction, but wasn't suspended.The man was initially removed by security, but the Fever's investigation determined that he did not violate the Fan Code of Conduct, and he returned to his seat. But the interaction reignited an always-simmering conversation about Fever fan behavior, one that has been ongoing since Caitlin Clark was drafted in 2024 and brought a wave of new fans to the league. Earlier this season, Phoenix Mercury forward Alyssa Thomas spoke out about receiving death threats after her hard foul on Clark in a game became national news.
Fever general manager Amber Cox gave an ardent defense of Fever fans."The attacks on our fanbase have no basis in reality, and they need to stop," Cox said on Saturday. "I'm talking about media who have never been to a game at Gainbridge Fieldhouse. Every organization in the league, every organization throughout professional sports, all the way down to youth rec leagues, have to deal with occasional bad behavior from spectators. And anyone who crosses the line in an arena or online needs to be held accountable. I want to be really clear about that. There is a line, and people need to be held accountable if they cross it."But here's the fact: We did not have one fan pointed out by a player who violated the WNBA code of conduct this season. Not one fan was removed from a game. ... Our fans love this team. They're going to cheer, they're going to boo, and sometimes they might point. It's a homecourt advantage for a reason, and it's the same for the Pacers. And all of that is within the code of conduct."
Brianna Turner, a forward for the Aces who played for the Fever in 2025, called Cox's quote about Fever fans "unequivocally false."
"This is an unequivocally false statement," Turner wrote on social media. "Players inside and outside the organization have repeatedly issued complaints with the Fever Fanbase. While it's not all Indy fans, it's certainly a trend. To say the attacks have 'no basis in reality' is disingenuous."

schema.headline: Fever players address additional public scrutiny of playing with Caitlin Clark, while GM defends fans - CBS Sports

title: Packers fear Edgerrin Cooper suffered torn Achilles in win over Buccaneers - CBS Sports
description: Matt LaFleur called the injury "not good" after the game,
body:
Matt LaFleur called the injury "not good" after the game, and the emerging defensive star is suspected to miss the rest of the year after being carted off against Tampa Bay
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Oct 4, 2026
                            
                    at
    5:18 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            1 min read
            
        
    

            
    
            
        
                
                
                
            
        
            
                    
                Getty Images
            
            

    
        Although the Packers secured a 17-14 win over the Buccaneers on Sunday, Green Bay suffered a big loss as well.While the injury is still being evaluated, the Packers fear that star third-year linebacker Edgerrin Cooper sustained a torn Achilles tendon against Tampa Bay, sources tell CBS Sports.Green Bay head coach Matt LaFleur confirmed CBS Sports' report during his postgame press conference, noting that Cooper's Achilles injury is "not good" and that he'd "suspect" it will be a season-ending injury.
The 24-year-old Cooper, a second-round draft pick in 2024 out of Texas A&M, had been continuing to emerge as one of the young linebackers in the NFL. After tallying 205 total tackles during his first two seasons with the Packers, Cooper had 30 tackles and three sacks through the first three-and-a-half games of this season before the injury.He had nine tackles and a sack Sunday against Tampa Bay before sustaining the injury and having to be carted off the field.
Green Bay, which improved to 2-2 with the win over the Buccaneers, faces the 3-1 Bears next week.

schema.headline: Packers fear Edgerrin Cooper suffered torn Achilles in win over Buccaneers - CBS Sports

title: Ravens' Lamar Jackson questionable to return after injury as Tyler Huntley steps in - CBS Sports
description: Tyler Huntley opened the second half at quarterback with B
body:
Tyler Huntley opened the second half at quarterback with Baltimore leading Tennessee 24-7
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Oct 4, 2026
                            
                    at
    4:56 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            1 min read
            
        
    

            
    
            
        
                
                
                
            
        
            
                    
                Getty Images
            
            

    
        Tyler Huntley started the second half of the Baltimore Ravens' Week 4, 24-18 victory against the Tennessee Titans, as Lamar Jackson suffered an ankle injury at the end of the second quarter. Jackson did not return. Jackson suffered the injury on the second-to-last play of the first half, when Jermaine Johnson II sacked him and appeared to twist his ankle. The two-time NFL MVP completed 15-of-20 passes for 222 yards and two touchdowns before exiting, to go along with 20 yards rushing. 
Head coach Jesse Minter told reporters after the game that the team doesn't know the extent of Jackson's ankle injury, but they did discuss allowing him to re-enter the game in the second half. NFL Network reports that Jackson is considered day-to-day and the Ravens will continue to monitor and treat him this week.Huntley completed 8-of-9 passes for 63 yards and rushed four times for 16 yards in the final two quarters, but the Ravens did not score any points. Derrick Henry led the offensive attack with 73 rushing yards and one touchdown on 23 carries vs. his former team. 
Jackson entered Sunday with 745 passing yards, four touchdowns and one interception through three weeks. He leads the league in yards per attempt (9.8) and yards per attempt off play-action (13.4).

title: Jalen Duren says he wants 'to be a Piston for life' despite contentious free agency, trade rumors - CBS Sports
description: Duren eventually accepted Detroit's five-year, $200 million offer, but not before leaks of a fractured team-playe
body:
Duren eventually accepted Detroit's five-year, $200 million offer, but not before leaks of a fractured team-player relationship
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Oct 4, 2026
                            
                    at
    4:21 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            3 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        As the months dragged on during the restricted free agency standoff between Jalen Duren and the Detroit Pistons, a pretty sensible question started to arise: did Duren even want to remain with the only NBA team he'd ever known? Duren reportedly felt immense disrespect at the offers the Pistons had made him. ESPN noted that "there were fractures built within the player-team relationship during the business of restricted free agency" and that Duren skipped media day and the beginning of training camp "hoping for a potential sign and trade." In the end, though, Duren elected to accept Detroit's final, increased offer of $200 million over five years.On Sunday, Duren addressed the media for the first time since the beginning of free agency. Questions justifiably remained even after he signed. Duren becomes trade-eligible on Jan. 15, and with teams like the Sacramento Kings reportedly open to giving him the full max offer that the Pistons ultimately didn't, the potential for a trade down the line still certainly exists. If it happens, though, Duren indicated that it won't be by his choice."The clearest message I can give today: I am a Detroit Piston and I want to be a Piston for life," Duren said at Sunday's press conference. He challenged the reporting by saying that "nothing came from me. Everything that was being heard was speculation."
Ultimately, the NBA is a business. The contracts Detroit offered Duren were something of a historical anomaly. As Nate Duncan noted, of the last 35 players to make an All-Star Team on their first contract, 34 of them received max contracts on their second. Duren is the outlier, and based on what he was eligible for, he didn't even come close. As an All-NBA player, Duren could have made up to $287 million on this contract through the Derrick Rose Rule. It is exceedingly rare that the young, All-NBA players are denied max deals, so it's hardly surprising that Duren would have felt disrespected by the lesser offers the Pistons put in front of him. That is especially true in light of the max offers he likely felt he could have gotten next summer as an unrestricted free agent. Such deals, through the four-year limitation on external suitors, the smaller annual raises available to those teams and the well-below-market qualifying offer salary Duren would have needed to take for a year to get there, would have ultimately paid him less than what Detroit ultimately offered, but there would have been no question about respect considering they would have paid him the maximum allowable amount.Detroit, meanwhile, wrestled with the new financial world NBA teams are living in. The 2023 CBA, through the aprons and a number of other rule changes, has created a far less forgiving cap environment. Get one contract wrong and the damage can cascade down to the entire rest of your roster. Had Duren's season ended in mid-April, he still might have gotten the max. But he also sorely underperformed in the postseason, raising questions about his long-term viability as one of Detroit's cornerstones.
"The way the season ended was humbling," Duren said on Sunday. "I need to get better. I looked in the mirror and realized I do need to get better. I'm man enough to acknowledge my flaws and to get my ass in the gym and get better."The onus will be on Duren to correct those postseason issues to an extent. There are also questions of roster fit that the Pistons need to consider. Two of Detroit's three most important players -- Duren and Ausar Thompson -- are complete non-threats from 3-point range. Both signed five-year deals this offseason. The two may not be offensively compatible in an era in which proper spacing is a necessity.If Detroit believed that with any certainty, it would have more seriously considered sign-and-trades this offseason. The Pistons want to give this another go. If another playoff run or two proves that the roster needs significant changes, Detroit can make them down the line. For now, their priority was keeping a 22-year-old All-NBA player in the building. It took some heated negotiations, but with the dust settled, all parties involved seem ready to move on and try to make up for last spring's disappointment.

schema.headline: Jalen Duren says he wants 'to be a Piston for life' despite contentious free agency, trade rumors - CBS Sports

title: Five-star Jordan Page commits to UConn: Dan Hurley lands another 2027 prize recruit - CBS Sports
description: Dan Hurley and the Huskies earned Page's pledge over finalists North Carolina, NC State and others
body:
Dan Hurley and the Huskies earned Page's pledge over finalists North Carolina, NC State and others
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Oct 4, 2026
                            
                    at
    1:25 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            1 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        UConn and Dan Hurley have added another five-star standout to their 2027 recruiting class. On Sunday, wing Jordan Page announced on Sunday his commitment to the Huskies, giving one of college basketball's top programs another top prospect to build around.The 6-foot-5, 210-pound wing from IMG Academy in Bradenton, Fla. hails from North Carolina and is ranked No. 10 overall in his class and the third-best player at his position per 247Sports. Page is the second five-star to commit to the Huskies this cycle, joining combo guard NaVorro Bowman Jr., who announced his decision last month. Page took official visits in September to North Carolina and UConn before making his decision. The Tar Heels were the early favorite to land Page, before the Huskies thoroughly impressed the gifted athlete during his visit to Hurley's program.
Adam Finkelstein, CBS Sports' Director of Basketball Scouting, says the lefty's best attributes are his length and two-way ability.The key for Page is playing within the flow offensively," Finkelstein wrote in his summer evaluation of the prospect. "He's more of a natural connector than offensive alpha. He doesn't have much wiggle off the dribble, needs to improve his right hand, isn't yet a secondary handler or overly polished at using ball screens and could better leverage his physical tools in the lane. "His shooting mechanics suffer, particularly with his footwork, when he starts settling for rushed or contested shots. In short, he projects as someone who should be capable of keeping the dominos falling once they start but is not yet a primary playmaker."
Finkelstein believes Page checks a lot of boxes that fit what Hurley wanst from his players at UConn."Page may be the best natural fit for what UConn emphasizes on a daily basis," Finkelstein wrote a 247Sports scout and fit article. "First, he checks all of the necessary boxes from a competitive character standpoint. The bar is high at UConn, in terms of what Hurley expects on a day-to-day basis, and Jordan is going to be able to meet that standard with the way he goes about his work."Secondly, he's a team-first player whose game is best suited when he is surrounded by other good players. He's not someone who is going to need a requisite number of shots or offensive volume, because he understands how to impact winning both with and without the basketball."

title: Brewers will have open stadium roof for NLDS Game 2 after controversial ending vs. Padres - CBS Sports
description: The roof will be open at American Family Field on Sunday afternoon as the Brewers try to take a 2-0 series lead
body:
The roof will be open at American Family Field on Sunday afternoon as the Brewers try to take a 2-0 series lead
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Oct 4, 2026
                            
                    at
    2:01 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            1 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        There will not be another roof-related controversy in Game 2 of the National League Division Series between the San Diego Padres and Milwaukee Brewers on Sunday. The American Family Field retractable roof will be open for the game, according to the team's roof hotline (yes, that is a real thing).The roof was closed for Game 1 on Saturday night, when Ty France's possible go-ahead home run hit a roof cable and was caught for an out in the ninth inning. The ground rules at American Family Field say that balls that hit the roof in fair territory are in play. France's ball hit the cable and was caught by Jackson Chourio for the second out of the ninth inning with the tying run on base.
The Padres had the play reviewed to check whether the ball struck the cable in fair or foul territory. It was determined it hit the cable in fair territory, so it was indeed a live ball and the second out of the inning. If it hit the cable in foul territory, it would have been a dead ball. The next batter, Jackson Merrill, lined out to right field to end the game (MIL 3, SD 2)."Unfortunately a bad break for us," Padres manager Craig Stammen said after Game 1. "Looked like it was a possible home run.  Just didn't go our way ... We should be able to bounce back just fine from it."   
All weather and roof-related decisions in the postseason are made by the commissioner's office in consultation with the home team and the umpire crew. The league typically errs on the side of caution in the postseason. If there is even the slightest chance of a weather delay or postponement, retractable roofs will be closed to avoid any disruptions.According to CBS local, it's a spectacular day for a ballgame in Milwaukee, with game time temperatures in the upper 60s and a light breeze, and few clouds. The weather forecast, moreso than avoiding another roof-related controversy, is the reason the roof will be open for Game 2. Temperatures were in the low 60s on Saturday night for Game 1.
The Brewers have a 1-0 lead in the best-of-five NLDS. Righties Logan Henderson and Michael King will be the starting pitchers for Game 2 on Sunday afternoon.

title: Bill Belichick joins Giants' 1986 reunion following North Carolina's loss to Notre Dame - CBS Sports
description: Belichick quickly revisited one of his biggest NFL moments
body:
Belichick quickly revisited one of his biggest NFL moments
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Oct 4, 2026
                            
                    at
    3:13 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            2 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        Members of the 1986 New York Giants gathered Saturday night for a dinner celebrating the 40th anniversary of the franchise's first Super Bowl win. The gathering included Bill Belichick, who arrived in New Jersey shortly after North Carolina's loss to Notre Dame. Belichick's evening included a picture with former Giants defenders Lawrence Taylor and Leonard Marshall. Belichick departed after the dinner and was not part of Sunday's halftime celebration honoring the '86 Giants. Now in his second season at North Carolina, Belichick made a name for himself with the Giants as the team's defensive coordinator from 1985-90. Over that span, the Giants won the franchise's first two Super Bowls largely on the strength of their defense. Belichick was carried off the field after the Giants blanked Washington in the 1986 NFC title game. In that year's Super Bowl, the Giants' defense recorded a massive goal-line stand that helped New York record a 39-20 win over John Elway's Broncos. 
In the 1990 NFC title game, Belichick's defense held the mighty 49ers offense to just 13 points, depriving San Francisco of a shot at becoming the first team to win three straight Super Bowls. Against Buffalo in that year's Super Bowl, Belichick crafted a game plan that focused on shutting down the Bills' explosive offense. While Thurman Thomas ran for 135 yards, Belichick's defense allowed just 19 points as the Giants' offense controlled the ball for a Super Bowl record 40 minutes and 33 seconds. The Giants' 20-19 win remains the only Super Bowl decided by a single point. Belichick, who later led the Patriots to a record six Super Bowl titles, enjoyed a successful partnership with then-Giants coach Bill Parcells, who in 1996 became the second coach to lead multiple franchises to Super Bowl appearances. Parcells was not feeling well and did not take part in the Giants' weekend festivities. Parcells, 85, recently gave an interview discussing the '86 Giants, in which he described his appreciation for Phil Simms, who won Super Bowl MVP that year after completing a record 88% of his passes against the Broncos. 
While Parcells was absent, many other members of the Giants took part in the celebration. 
The '86 Giants became the franchise's first championship team in 30 years. That season, the Giants went 17-2 while employing the league's second-best scoring defense and eighth-best scoring offense. In the postseason, the Giants outscored San Francisco, Washington and Denver by a combined score of 105-23. Belichick's appearance at the Giants' anniversary is notable for several reasons. One is that he has had little affiliation with the NFL since he and the Patriots parted ways after the 2023 season. Prior to becoming North Carolina's coach, Belichick spent a year in the media after he was not able to land another NFL head coaching opportunity. 
The Tar Heels went 4-8 during Belichick's first season in Chapel Hill. North Carolina split its first four games of the 2026 campaign.

schema.headline: Bill Belichick joins Giants' 1986 reunion following North Carolina's loss to Notre Dame - CBS Sports

title: Week 4 overreactions: Should Rams still be Super Bowl favorites? Cowboys to win NFC East? - CBS Sports
description: Sean McVay's visceral reaction to the Rams' 24-20 comeback win over the Eagles is one small part of what makes the NFL so great. Think t
body:
Sean McVay's visceral reaction to the Rams' 24-20 comeback win over the Eagles is one small part of what makes the NFL so great. Think these early-season games don't mean anything? Think winning a game you "should" win shouldn't elicit celebration? Think again.The margins in the NFL are tiny. Entering the late-afternoon window, seven of the 10 games played in Week 4 were decided by one possession. Another game — Cardinals at Giants — came down to the final snap, when Deonte Banks' pick six made it a multi-score game. Teeny, tiny differences matter so much.And that's why the Rams' win matters. The Super Bowl favorites were staring down a 1-3 start and a long, long list of questions. They still have questions, sure, but they'll feel a lot better addressing those questions after a win.And that's why you see McVay high-fiving his players and celebrating as if he had just won a Super Bowl — a celebration he has, in fact, done before. His reaction is an earned one, not an overreaction.
Speaking of overreactions — or not ...The Rams shouldn't be Super Bowl favoritesOverreaction or reality: OverreactionThere are two ways to view the Rams' 24-20 win over the injury-ravaged Eagles:Wow, that was super unimpressive.Wow, that was an impressive comeback.It can be both. Los Angeles struggling to beat a Philadelphia team without DeVonta Smith, Saquon Barkley, Quinyon Mitchell, Zack Baun, Lane Johnson, Landon Dickerson and others was a bad look ... for 52-plus minutes.But the last 7:26? Super impressive:10-play, 98-yard touchdown driveForced a three-and-out10-play, 79-yard touchdown driveForced a turnover on downsMatthew Stafford, against Eagles' defensive coordinator Vic Fangio and in the rain, struggled. Those are two factors he has always struggled with. In fact, this was his first win over a Fangio-coached defense. But when the Rams had to have it, they got Stafford at his best: 12-for-15 for 140 yards over the two late, lengthy scoring drives. Kyren Williams pounded in two touchdowns.The score will lie about who dominated this game. The Rams had 415 yards of offense and averaged 5.4 yards per play, compared to 172 and 3.0, respectively, for Philadelphia. The Rams committed some horrible turnovers and penalties, but on a play-by-play basis, they were far superior. Puka Nacua had nine catches for 125 yards and ran for a score. They won without Myles Garrett, Aaron Donald and Jaylen Watson on defense. This was a crucial, crucial win, and one that should only prove Los Angeles can win when so much goes wrong.
The Cowboys will win the NFC EastOverreaction or reality: RealitySpeaking of important wins, the Cowboys just got their most important since the 2023 season: Dallas 34, Houston 30.This game had a little bit of everything and a lot of one thing in particular: CeeDee Lamb. He had 17 catches for 189 yards and a touchdown against the Texans' normally terrific defense. He was unstoppable everywhere, a true superstar at his peak. Dak Prescott was absolutely outstanding with 335 passing yards, a touchdown (to Lamb, naturally) and no interceptions or fumbles.The issues in the secondary remain, but the Cowboys held the Texans to a 31.6% rushing success rate. That is Dallas' second-lowest rate allowed this season. Yes, I know it's the Texans, but it's a start.
This is a game the Cowboys needed to win, and they found a way to do so. Looking around the division, the Eagles' offense remains a mess, the Giants are 3-1 but not likely to threaten with Jameis Winston under center, and the Commanders are in a world of trouble.Simply put, Dallas, with a defense that should only improve and an offense that can go toe-to-toe with any, should win this division. If it can't, there should be major questions from the top down ... again.The Jaguars should be the AFC favoriteOverreaction or reality: OverreactionHo hum. Another week, another win for the Jaguars, who have won 11 of their last 12 regular-season games going back to last year. This time, it was a 22-17 win over the Bengals in Cincinnati. Yes, the Bengals lost Ja'Marr Chase to a concussion early in the game, but this is a really impressive win over another AFC team with playoff aspirations.
Trevor Lawrence had another strong game — 18-for-23 for 227 yards (9.9 yards per attempt) with a touchdown and no interceptions — and the Jaguars ran for 111 yards while allowing just 23. Foyesade Oluokun and Jourdan Lewis both picked off Joe Burrow.DraftKings has the Jaguars with the fourth-shortest odds to win the AFC (+590), behind the Ravens (+390), Bills (+395) and Chiefs (+405). The Jaguars probably belong among those teams, but not as the definitive favorite. It's a crowded group, and that doesn't even include the Broncos or Patriots.Two things can be true: The Jaguars look like the best team in the AFC right now, and I'm not sure I would take them as my pick to represent the AFC in the Super Bowl at the moment.
Still, it's absurd how much they're being overlooked. Only the 49ers have a better line-of-scrimmage expected points added, and they've played a much easier schedule. This is a really, really good team.The Packers are back on track for playoff contentionOverreaction or reality: OverreactionThe Packers eked out a 17-14 win over the Buccaneers to get to 2-2 on the season, but major problems persist.Jordan Love threw an awful interception late in the game that gave the Buccaneers life.Kaleb Johnson had a red zone fumble.The rushing game was better — a season-high 40% rushing success rate — but still not good. Factor in the Johnson fumble, and the Packers still had a -0.25 EPA per rush.The Buccaneers, playing with an undrafted rookie backup quarterback, posted a 54% rushing success rate and racked up 141 rushing yards.And in new negative developments, CBS Sports' Matt Zenitz reports that the Packers fear standout linebacker Edgerrin Cooper has torn his Achilles.
The biggest positive for Green Bay (after winning the game, of course) was that Love took no sacks. The offensive line was much better. But this team is still miles away from looking like a playoff contender, and that goes for both sides of the ball.Ben Johnson will win Coach of the YearOverreaction or reality: OverreactionBen Johnson should be the frontrunner for Coach of the Year. He's now won games with Caleb Williams, Tyson Bagent and Case Keenum ... and it's only Week 4! According to CBS Sports research, only one other team has had three different quarterbacks throw for 200+ yards in a win through four weeks: the 1997 Jaguars.Unfortunately for Johnson's Coach of the Year candidacy, the award tends to go to a coach whose team way overachieves: Mike Vrabel's Patriots last year, Kevin O'Connell's Vikings (with Sam Darnold) in 2024, Kevin Stefanski's Browns in 2023, Brian Daboll's Giants in 2022.
Basically, the external preseason expectations were likely too high for Johnson and the Bears for him to win the award this year, even if you could argue he's been the best coach in the sport so far. Dan Quinn belongs on the hot seatOverreaction or reality: RealityThere are a lot of things Dan Quinn cannot control. He can't control that Jayden Daniels is hurt, nor that Marcus Mariota got hurt Sunday, forcing the Commanders to turn to seventh-round rookie Athan Kaliakmanis under center. He cannot control that the team has injuries pretty much everywhere up and down the roster. He can't control a litany of other problems, including that there simply isn't enough talent, period.But the things he can control aren't going his way, either. The biggest mistake in Sunday's 30-13 loss to the Colts in London was going for a fourth-and-1 in his own territory late in the first half. At the time, the Commanders were leading 6-0. The defense was dominant, forcing two Daniel Jones turnovers. A punt would have been the easy answer, especially with a third-string rookie at quarterback.
Instead, the Commanders failed on a mess of a play, giving the Colts the spark they needed. Indianapolis scored a touchdown and never trailed again.Washington is also one of the most penalized teams in the NFL. Now 1-3 with a ton of tough matchups upcoming, the Commanders face a must-win against the Giants in Week 5.

schema.headline: Week 4 overreactions: Should Rams still be Super Bowl favorites? Cowboys to win NFC East? - CBS Sports

title: Odell Beckham Jr. breaks silence after being released by New York Giants - CBS Sports
description: In his first public comments since being released, Beckham said the Giants "won" from the attention surrounding h
body:
In his first public comments since being released, Beckham said the Giants "won" from the attention surrounding his return
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Oct 4, 2026
                            
                    at
    1:38 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            3 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        The New York Giants put an end to one of the feel-good storylines of the early NFL season when they released wide receiver Odell Beckham Jr. OBJ, who turns 34 next month, returned to the Giants this offseason and earned a spot on the final 53-man roster. However, he didn't see much playing time in the first three weeks of the season.OBJ played a grand total of 20 offensive snaps through three games and recorded zero receptions. Giants fans hoped to witness a storybook end to his NFL career. During New York's Week 3 victory over the Tennessee Titans last Sunday, "OBJ" chants could be heard throughout MetLife Stadium. However, the Giants decided to cut ties with him.  Given OBJ's legendary status, this rubbed some people the wrong way. One football fan made an Instagram video insulting John Harbaugh, Joe Schoen and the Giants organization for using OBJ to make money -- bringing him in to create a storyline and drum up fan interest with zero intent to actually use him. Beckham actually commented on the video and seemed to agree with the creator, "realbcasbreaks." In what may be his first public comments since he was released, OBJ said the Giants "won" given the attention he brought while accepting a veteran minimum contract. He even said he "shoulda known better."
"Im super smart !!!! But I didn't see this one my brotha! They got me!!! They won on top of the money u talkin bout I made tnem I came in HUMBLY took vet min then EARNED my spot n didn't say nothing bout no $$$ which I kno make for everybody 🤑🤑… Ima tell u this ima grown man and this Shxt didn't hurt me but it did when they cut me like that cause part of me is like I shoulda known better. Now let me tellllll u the realllll deal truth what hurt my heart to the core is comin home and seeing my son and how happy he was with no idea of what happened and talkin bout my job n jersey number 13 broke me tf down.. funny thing about that is he said he likes 3 better n I find that very interesting .. but again there was no real pain till u get home and ur son gives u that hug like idc what happened daddy ur the best and I love u… nothing better than tht.. but yea idk why they even gave me the run along I coulda really been playing this year somewhere and making a impact and I mean that from a person whose humbled by God and life, so all im doin is gettin ready for whatever God has for me and spreading luv n meantime."The Giants replaced Beckham by signing wide receiver and punt returner Braxton Berrios to the active roster, along with Charlie Jones. Harbaugh addressed Beckham's release this week, saying that it just "wasn't working for us." "I had a great conversation with Odell, and it's tough," Harbaugh said, via SNY. "But we just weren't getting enough, you know? It just wasn't working for us. And like I told him, I wanted to be able to get more. I wanted him to be able to do more, I wanted to get him on the field more. Whatever reason, we weren't able to do it. Put it on us. We weren't able to get it done. But at this point in time, that's kind of where we were and we needed to move on."While there's no disputing that the signing of OBJ excited the fan base, it remains to be seen what kind of impact he can have at this stage of his career. He hasn't crossed 55 yards receiving in a season since 2023 with the Baltimore Ravens. Beckham spent one year with the Miami Dolphins in 2024, and then went unsigned in 2025 while being suspended six games for violating the NFL's policies on performance-enhancing drugs. 
Time will tell if Beckham catches on with another team. For a few potential landing spots, click here.

title: NFL Week 4 winners and losers: Drake Maye, Patriots shine as Texans fall to 0-4 - CBS Sports
description: Maye rediscovered his 2025 form against the Bills, while Houston's latest loss left its playoff hopes hanging by
body:
Maye rediscovered his 2025 form against the Bills, while Houston's latest loss left its playoff hopes hanging by a thread
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Oct 4, 2026
                            
                    at
    6:22 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            6 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        A pair of reigning playoff teams from the AFC needed to get up off the mat in Week 4. One side did so in resounding fashion while the other suffered the kind of loss that could effectively end its hunt for a return to the postseason. The New England Patriots took down the conference's best team for a get-right win, and the team they beat in last year's divisional round, the Houston Texans, fell to 0-4 to continue a miserable start to the season.That dichotomy underscores how high the stakes are as the 2026 season enters its first month. This is one of those weeks when the NFL learns which teams are for real and which are bound to compete at the bottom of the league ladder. The separation built between Super Bowl hopefuls and No. 1 draft pick contenders on Sunday was eye-opening.Week 4 has also been a brutal one from an injury standpoint. Players, unfortunately, get hurt every week. But the name value of those who dropped out of action this weekend was as significant as that of any of the previous three slates of games.Here are the NFL's biggest winners and losers from Week 4.
                            
    
                                                
                    
    Winner: Drake Maye and the PatriotsThere might have been no bigger disappointment across the NFL through three games than Drake Maye, whose regression from MVP runner-up to the league's second-worst quarterback by passer rating was a puzzling fall from grace. The 2025 version of Maye reappeared in the New England Patriots' 29-26 upset of the Buffalo Bills. He passed for 269 yards and three touchdowns and led the Patriots in rushing with another 54 yards.
Losing A.J. Brown to a high ankle sprain in Week 1 seemed to throw Maye off. His return is near, but importantly, Maye might have finally found a groove with his other targets. He spread the ball around to seven receivers on Sunday, tossed a pair of touchdowns to Romeo Doubs and got a little help from Efton Chism III on a one-handed catch for what proved to be the game-winning score. This should be a major confidence builder for a quarterback who could not get out of his own way to begin the year.Maye's rounding into form is, of course, a crucial development for a Patriots team that could have ill-afforded to drop into a 1-3 hole. Getting up off the mat on the heels of a blowout loss was important, and doing it against the Bills was a best-case scenario, considering Buffalo is arguably the best team in the NFL and the Patriots' stiffest AFC East competition.
                            
    
                                                
                    
    Loser: TexansSince the Houston Texans reversed course last year to reach the playoffs after an 0-3 start, hardly anyone fully counted them out when they lost the first three games in 2026. But now? A 34-30 loss to the Dallas Cowboys leaves minimal room for optimism.
Defense was supposed to be Houston's calling card this year. It certainly was not on Sunday when it surrendered three touchdowns to Javonte Williams in the second half alone and had no answers for CeeDee Lamb. The Cowboys' star wide receiver racked up 17 catches to finish just one grab behind Jason Witten for the single-game franchise record, and he did it against what should be one of the NFL's stingiest defensive backfields. The Texans were no stalwarts on that side of the ball in any of their previous three losses, either.Houston should finally grab its first win of the campaign next week when it meets the Tennessee Titans in a matchup of two winless AFC South teams. It might, however, already be too late to save a disastrous start to the year.
                            
    
                                                
                    
    Loser: Commanders quarterbacksFans in London did not have much reason to cheer for the Washington Commanders in Sunday's international game. The Indianapolis Colts pulled away from them in a 30-13 rout at Tottenham Hotspur Stadium and did so comfortably as it was clear the Commanders would not be able to maintain pace once Marcus Mariota went down with a game-ending knee injury. Washington took a 6-0 lead with him on the field and was outscored 30-7 from that point forward.
Rookie Athan Kaliakmanis, out of Rutgers, stepped into action and completed just 15 of 33 passes with a touchdown and an interception in his professional regular-season debut. He also took a sack and sustained multiple hard hits. The Commanders are stretched so thin at quarterback that if Kaliakmanis left the game for any reason, tight end Colson Yankoff would have had to step in as the emergency signal-caller.Moving forward, the Commanders will either have a backup quarterback on the field or a less-than-healthy Jayden Daniels. There is no telling how effective he will be when he comes back from his elbow injury, which will require offseason surgery and which forces him to play with a brace on his non-throwing arm.
                            
    
                                                
                    
    Winner: Jets defenseCoach Aaron Glenn, the New York Jets defensive personnel, and their frustrated fanbase can finally sleep easily. To whatever extent possible, at least, in the wake of a 23-12 loss to the Chicago Bears. They undoubtedly would have preferred a win, but they did get a huge monkey off their back in the second quarter of that defeat when five-time Pro Bowl safety Minkah Fitzpatrick picked off Tyson Bagent for the franchise's first interception in 637 days. At long last, the drought is over.
The 20 games New York went between interceptions was an NFL record. It was a defining element of the team's defensive ineptitude last year and carried over into the first month of 2026, even as the unit showed modest signs of improvement. What remains clear is that there is still a lot of work to be done on that side of the ball, considering the takeaway was not enough to keep Chicago and its backup quarterback in check.
                            
    
                                                
                    
    Loser: Eagles third-down offenseThe Philadelphia Eagles made the wrong kind of franchise history in Week 4 with the worst third-down execution in their 94 years of existence. Never before had the offense gone 0-12 in third-down situations until Sunday's 24-20 loss to the Los Angeles Rams. Making matters worse, the Eagles found it difficult to move the chains on fourth down, too, with just one conversion on four tries. Those three turnovers on downs were costly in their scoreless second half.First-year offensive coordinator Sean Mannion was always going to be heavily scrutinized this season because of the high-pressure situation he walked into. Sunday's performance was no resounding endorsement of his scheme nor his play-calling abilities. Perhaps it speaks more to Jalen Hurts and his shortcomings, though. Or maybe it was a product of Saquon Barkley missing nearly the entire game with a hamstring injury.
Regardless of who is most to blame, the Eagles cost themselves this game. They held a 10-point lead with four minutes to play and lost because they could not tack onto their advantage in the second half and could not stay on the field to drain the clock in the final period.Loser: Superstar healthBarkley is not the only household name who departed from action in Week 4. Lamar Jackson also missed the second half of the Baltimore Ravens' victory with an ankle issue, and Ja'Marr Chase suffered a concussion in the second quarter of the Cincinnati Bengals' loss. Barkley, Jackson and Chase are all at least top-three players at the most high-profile positions in football and were not on the field for most of the day. That is a tough blow for them, their teams and every football fan everywhere.It is not immediately clear whether Barkley will miss additional time. Chase will have to clear the NFL's concussion protocol before he returns. Jackson is considered day-to-day in the early aftermath of his injury, which is a promising update that could make him available in Week 5.

title: Ja'Marr Chase injury update: Bengals WR ruled out with concussion - CBS Sports
description: Chase suffered a nasty hit during the second quarter
body:
Chase suffered a nasty hit during the second quarter
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Oct 4, 2026
                            
                    at
    2:48 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            1 min read
            
        
    

            
    
            
        
                
                
                
            
        
            
                    
                Getty Images
            
            

    
        Bengals star receiver Ja'Marr Chase sustained a crushing hit during the first half of Sunday's game against the Jaguars. Chase was ruled as out for the remainder for the game after he was initially ruled as questionable to return. Chase had his facemask twisted by Jarrian Jones before a hard hit from Ventrell Miller. Jones received a penalty on the play. Oddly, Miller was not penalized for using the crown of his helmet. 
Chase remained on the ground for several moments and was treated on the field by members of the Bengals' medical staff. He was able to walk off the field under his own power. Chase then went into the blue tent before walking into the locker room with a towel covering his head.   A Pro Bowler in each of his first six NFL seasons, Chase caught 18 passes for 185 yards and three touchdowns during the Bengals' first three games. He caught 9 of 12 targets for 98 yards and a score during last week's 30-27 loss to the Steelers. Chase caught each of his three targets for 26 yards on Sunday prior to the injury. 
The Bengals, who trailed 3-0 at the time of the injury, finished that drive with a game-tying field goal by Evan McPherson. Cincinnati trailed Jacksonville 13-3 at halftime.

It was at No. 8 in the Coaches Poll, and there was hope of a College Football Playoff run.Then the Gators went into Columbia and got a serious reality check from Missouri in the form of a 45-17 loss. Jadan Baugh, a Heisman Trophy contender just days ago, rushed for 13 yards on 12 carries. Tigers quarterback Austin Simmons dismantled the Florida secondary for 340 yards and a pair of touchdowns.As a result of that lopsided loss, the Gators tumbled down to No. 15 in the Coaches Poll. The Tigers, meanwhile, flew up to No. 16, where they inexplicably remain behind Florida.Another team that came back to Earth a bit was Mississippi State, which got a taste of the SEC's elite tier in a 56-23 loss to Alabama. title: Travis Kelce career receptions: Chiefs star closing in on top five of NFL all-time list - CBS Sports
description: Kelce is tied with Tim Brown for seventh in NFL history and needs nine catches to take sole possession of fifth p
body:
Kelce is tied with Tim Brown for seventh in NFL history and needs nine catches to take sole possession of fifth place
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Oct 4, 2026
                            
                    at
    12:45 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            2 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        Kansas City Chiefs star Travis Kelce is already among the greatest tight ends in NFL history, and this week, he will likely make his already impressive resume that much more convincing. Kelce is tied with wideout Tim Brown for the seventh-most receptions in NFL history with 1,094, meaning one catch from quarterback Patrick Mahomes and he will have sole possession of that mark.The Chiefs face the 3-0 Las Vegas Raiders and their strong pass defense, which is tied for the sixth-fewest completions allowed in the league (59). Cris Carter is No. 6 on the all-time list with 1,101 receptions, just seven more than Kelce. Marvin Harrison is at No. 5 with 1,102, eight more than Kelce. When he hits nine more catches, Kelce will be at No. 5 on his own. He could move multiple spots this week and has the chance to move up to No. 5. If he doesn't get it done this week, it should only take a few weeks for him to be in the top 5. RankPlayerReceptionsHow many more receptions than Kelce1Jerry Rice1,5494552Larry Fitzgerald1,4323383Tony Gonzalez1,3252314Jason Witten1,2281345Marvin Harrison1,10286Cris Carter1,1017(t)7Tim Brown1,094--(t)7Travis Kelce1,094--Predicting when Kelce will move up to No. 5In Week 1 against the Miami Dolphins, Kelce recorded two receptions on two targets. He registered nine receptions on 11 targets in Week 2 against the Indianapolis Colts, and caught three more balls on five targets in Week 3 against the Denver Broncos. He has 14 receptions total in the three wins, for an average of 4.6 catches per game.
If Kelce continues his trend of average receptions per game, he will pass Carter in Week 5 and will pass Harrison in Week 6. That said, the veteran always has a chance to have a big game and get those would-be historic receptions earlier. How far Kelce can move up on the list this yearIf Kelce continues to average 4.6 receptions per game, he will finish the year with 78 catches if he plays all 17 games at the average. That would put him at 1,172 all-time, which would still put him at No. 5, as Jason Witten has 1,228 at No. 4.To reach No. 4, Kelce needs 134 catches. The most receptions he has recorded in a single year is 110, and his 17-game average is 95 a year. If he plays in 2027 and continues at a similar level, he would likely pass Witten sometime next season.
At 36, Kelce will be hanging up the cleats sooner rather than later. While he hasn't announced whether he will retire after this year, after 14 seasons, it wouldn't come as a shock.
